questions.q: Discuss the causes of the Revolt of 1857.
answer: The Revolt of 1857 was the result of long-building discontent with British rule, sparked by a military grievance.

answer.text: British expansion through annexations, especially the Doctrine of Lapse and the seizure of Awadh in 1856, angered rulers and nobles who lost their thrones and pensions.
Heavy land revenue ruined peasants, while cheap British imports destroyed the livelihood of artisans and craftsmen, spreading distress in town and country.
Many Indians feared that the British aimed to interfere with their religion and convert them to Christianity, and resented certain social reforms as attacks on custom.
The introduction of the new Enfield rifle, whose cartridges were rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat, offended both Hindu and Muslim sepoys and provided the spark at Meerut in May 1857.

answer: Thus political, economic, social and military grievances together produced the great revolt.
